title: Cross-source claim deduplication and independent corroboration v0
problem: Blocked by ticket-419. Duplicate pages, versions, or repeated statements from one study can inflate support counts and graph confidence. The engine needs domain-neutral proposition normalization and source-family independence before graph completeness or retrieval quality can be trusted.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted claims receive a versioned normalized proposition key that preserves scope, population, outcome, direction, and material qualifiers.
Exact and near-duplicate claims are linked without deleting provenance or collapsing contradictory scopes.
Source-family identity distinguishes mirrors, preprint/published versions, and repeated pages of one study from genuinely independent sources using deterministic metadata when available.
Relationship support and score reconciliation count independent source families separately from raw claim count and cannot gain confidence solely from duplicates.
Rejected and needs-review candidates never contribute to deduplication clusters used by graph confidence.
Tests cover equivalent wording, conflicting direction, different populations, duplicate URLs, preprint/version pairs, and two genuinely independent studies.
On completion, ticket-421 changes from blocked to ready; no later Phase 4 ticket is activated.
test_plan: With mock-only env: python -m pytest tests/unit/test_claim_deduplication.py tests/unit/test_independent_corroboration.py -q
With mock-only env: python -m pytest tests/golden -q
With mock-only env: python -m rge.cli verify --skip-site
non_goals: Do not auto-merge claim rows or discard source-specific quotes.
Do not use embeddings until the retrieval embedding ticket.
Do not treat citation count as independent corroboration.
Do not rewrite historical score events destructively.
rollback_plan: Stop using proposition and source-family fields in scoring while retaining non-destructive linkage tables. Historical claims, quotes, relationships, and score events remain intact.
